artists.biography: Dead Cross emerged out of a series of impractical schemes, fallen-through plans, and last-minute musical experimentation. Shows were scheduled before a single song was written, fans were formed before even one show was played. The chaos of its creation seems apt; after all, the band is comprised entirely of artists who have thrived playing tightly-coiled turmoil—intelligent dissonance disguised as disorder. Consisting of Dave Lombardo, Justin Pearson, Michael Crain, and Mike Patton, the impressive, expansive, and eclectic list of prior bands collectively played in would be enough to ensure the unyielding ferocity of the music... but a resume isn’t necessary, here. Dead Cross stands on its own, speaks volumes with its multilayered evil-genius vocals, manic guitar riffs, and brutal rhythms. Read more on Last.fm. perplexity.description:
Dead Cross's second album, II, released in October 2022, represents the hardcore punk outfit's return after a five-year hiatus from their chaotic 2017 self-titled debut. The project reunites vocalist Mike Patton, former Slayer drummer Dave Lombardo, The Locust's Justin Pearson, and Pearson's Retox bandmate Michael Crain to deliver another uncompromising assault of noisy, thrashy hardcore. Rather than adopting a somber tone following Michael Crain's cancer diagnosis and the death of former member Gabe Serbian, the band instead intensified their approach, channeling these circumstances into a visceral and relentless sonic experience.

The album's 33-minute runtime showcases Dead Cross at their most frenetic, with tracks like the mesmeric opener "Love Without Love," the theatrical punk drive of "Animal Espionage," and the sub-two-minute blast of "Reign of Error" exemplifying the band's refusal to settle into conventional structures. The record maintains the chaotic, noisy aesthetic that defined their debut while demonstrating the collective's continued mastery of controlled mayhem. Patton's presence remains the defining element, his relentless vocal mania elevating the instrumental bedlam into something distinctly ambitious despite the project's straightforward hardcore classification.

II received favorable critical reception, with reviewers praising the band's willingness to embrace unpredictability and sonic intensity. The album solidified Dead Cross as a vital force in contemporary hardcore, proving that their debut was no anomaly but rather the beginning of a sustained artistic vision that prioritizes uncompromising creativity over accessibility.
